Bug: the owner said one sentence ("it's quite buggy") during voice dictation and it rendered 4 times in the chat. Root cause, confirmed by investigation: chat.js's draw() dedups line.chat entries against a seen_chat/own_ats set (around lines 245-263), but line.refined (returns early around line 253, before the dedup check) and line.para (around line 247) are NOT deduped — every line is delivered twice (Session.watch() 1.5s poll + Session.stream() SSE push), and if the chat widget is mounted in two places at once that doubles again to 4x. Widget.js's draw_refined() (lines ~520-537) also unconditionally inserts a new <details> node every call with no existing-node check, compounding it.

Fix: extend the existing seen_chat dedup (keyed by the line's `at`) in chat.js's draw() to also cover line.refined and line.para before they reach panel.say()/draw_refined() — same treatment as line.chat already gets. Also make Widget.js's draw_refined() check for an existing node for that `at` before inserting, as a second line of defense. Verify by loading a voice session page and confirming a refined readback renders only once.

Re-send: the duplicate-chat-line fix queued a few minutes ago (asked_at 2026-10-04T19:04:50.684-05:00) hasn't landed yet and the owner is still seeing duplicate messages live. Please pick it up now — see line 3 of public/framework/ai/quick-fix/page.jsonl for the full fix description (chat.js draw() dedup needs to cover line.refined and line.para, plus Widget.js draw_refined() needs an existing-node check).

Root cause confirmed for tonight's beeping/fallback/no-send bugs (all three tie back to AudioWorklet failures):

(a) Silent Chrome fallback: Dictate.detect_engine() (Dictate.js:263-269) only pings whisper-server's HTTP health endpoint, never whether ctx.audioWorklet.addModule(".../pcm-worklet.js") (capture.js:58) will actually succeed. If that throws AbortError, start_whisper() rejects, caught generically in start() (Dictate.js:349-354) -> set_error(). Next mic press, detect_engine() may briefly read whisper as unreachable and silently fall back to "browser" engine. Only visible sign is small muted text next to the mic button (name_engine(), Dictate.js:274-276) — too easy to miss. Fix: surface engine state prominently (not just muted text) and/or have detect_engine() also probe audioWorklet.addModule() so a worklet-load failure doesn't masquerade as "browser mode chosen normally."

(b) Extra/mistimed beeps: Mic.js's watch_capture() (Mic.js:460-473) listens for the mic track's "ended" event and reacts by calling stop() (beeps "stop") then, 400ms later, start() again (beeps "start" via on_listening(), Mic.js:449-450) — outside the owner's control. A failing AudioWorklet or a dying track fires "ended" repeatedly, producing the mid-utterance start/stop beep pairs. Fix: don't auto-beep on every watch_capture-triggered restart, or debounce/suppress the beep pair when it's an automatic recovery rather than a real user-initiated stop/start.

(c) Stop beep without actual send: the real "send on pause" logic (send_screen()/send_sentences()/flush_held()) only runs inside Mic.js's stop() override's finally block (Mic.js:724-742). But the stop beep is ALSO fired independently from set_error() (Mic.js:477-481), called directly from several error paths (Dictate.start()'s catch, close_segment()'s whisper-unreachable catch at Dictate.js:566-575, the browser 6s-silence watchdog) — none of which go through stop(). So a worklet/track failure that ends the session via set_error() plays the stop beep but never reaches the send code. Fix: make set_error()'s error paths also flush/send pending text (or call through stop()'s send logic) before/while playing the stop beep, so a beep never fires without the matching send.

Please fix all three in order of annoyance: (b) the beeping first since it's the most disruptive, then (c) the missing send, then (a) making the engine-fallback visible. Verify by forcing a worklet load failure (or just load the Dictate page with whisper-server down) and confirming: no beep storm, a pause still sends, and the engine badge clearly shows "browser fallback".

Owner clarified the exact beep UX spec for the Dictate mic (refines the queued beeping/no-send fix on this same page):

- Beep ONLY on a real start/stop: the owner tapping the mic on/off, or the mic auto-starting as a result of a deliberate user action (tapping "new card", opening the AI mobile rail button, etc).
- NEVER beep mid-transcription from an internal/automatic restart (e.g. watch_capture()'s "ended" event triggering stop()+start() on its own, Mic.js:460-473) — that's the annoying mid-utterance beep storm. An automatic recovery restart should be silent.
- On auto-send (the silence-triggered send after a pause), play a distinct SEND sound (different from the mic start/stop beep) and clear the text area — owner explicitly confirmed this is the UX they want: like a walkie-talkie/audiobook feel, a clear "heard you, sent" cue.

So: three distinct sounds/behaviors — user-initiated start beep, user-initiated stop beep, and a separate auto-send chime + clear-textarea — and automatic internal restarts get no sound at all. Please fold this into the fix already queued for the worklet-triggered beep storm and missing auto-send.

BUG, urgent (owner): the "today" button on /framework/ai/sessions/ loads TOMORROW after ~7pm local, because AISessionsPage.js uses UTC dates. Fix in public/framework/ai/AISession/AISessionsPage.js: import Day from "/framework/core/Session/Day.js" and make every date local: `static ymd(d){ return Day.path(d); }`, `static month_of(d){ return Day.of(d).slice(0, 7); }`, line 66 `this.date_to = Day.of(today);`, line 68 the default from = the earlier of the 1st of this LOCAL month and 6 days ago, as Day.of strings (no Date.UTC, no toISOString), line 242 "show 30 more days" `Day.of(Date.parse(this.date_from) - 30 * 864e5)` — careful, Date.parse of a bare YYYY-MM-DD is UTC midnight, so parse it as local (new Date(y, m-1, d)) first. grep the file for getUTC|toISOString and leave none that compute a day. Proof: at 21:00 local on 2026-10-20 the today button shows 2026-10-20 sessions (check_page /framework/ai/sessions/?scope=2026-10-20 at 1200 shows rows). Merge.

The owner (2026-10-24, prompt log ai/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/page.jsonl line 403): "The top tabs ... on the framework slash AI page. There's a series of top tabs. On mobile, those tabs wrap ... we want them to side scroll. I want the icon and the title to remain in place. I don't want that to side scroll. I want only the tabs themselves to side scroll. It'll extend off screen and then you can use horizontal swiping on mobile. Hopefully that will work fine on desktop as well." = the AI section's header tab bar (INBOX DASHBOARD LOG QUEUE TASKS SYSTEM SESSIONS TESTS beside the robot icon + "AI" title): one row, never wrap; the tab strip alone scrolls horizontally (overflow-x auto, touch swipe), icon + title fixed. Check with shots at 390 px and 1920 px; land in a worktree, ready to merge.

Follow-up to your 2865590d4 fix (the owner, 2026-10-24): "the top tabs are now on one line. They are wrapping still, like they're not next to the header. I kind of like having the tabs and the heading, the icon heading, all on the same line. And then have the tab area be swipeable." So, at every width including phones: the robot icon + "AI" heading and the tab strip share ONE row. The heading keeps its size (flex: none), and the tab strip takes the rest (flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow-x: auto; no wrap), so it swipes sideways and runs off the right edge. Shots at 390 and 1920. Note: the page mastermind will later make this row sticky, so keep it a plain flex row.

The owner (2026-10-24, again): "the header fix for the top tabs is still not in... the robot icon and the AI title are on their own line with a bunch of empty space to the right, and the tabs wrap to their own line below it. I want the AI title and the top tabs on the same line. Their parent container needs to be flex... grouped properly so it doesn't break the items below." Your 8abde71b5 fix works on /framework/ai/queue/ (checked at 390 and 1400), but NOT on the pages the owner is on: /framework/ai/sessions/ and the session detail page /framework/ai/sessions/e00f55c9-bad4-4ee2-899e-d629ea1eede6/ (and likely other AI pages). Find the header those pages use (it may be a different class or wrapper), and make icon + title + tabs one flex row there too, on every AI page. Note that a headless shot of the sessions pages never reaches networkidle (live sockets), so shoot with waitUntil: domcontentloaded plus a short wait. Check at 390 and 1920.

The small 'newest' button with the down arrow in the chat (Chat v2 / the voice sheet) is quite broken, and the chat is not scrolling properly (scroll lock / pin to bottom). Take a screenshot of it, find the cause and fix it. If it is bigger than a quick fix, start a task mastermind.

Newest button scroll bug: clicking the down-arrow 'newest' button aligns the LAST message to the TOP of the scrollable chat area, but it lands about a whole screen off so nothing is visible. It should scroll so the last message sits at the BOTTOM of the visible chat area (scroll to scrollHeight / scrollIntoView block:'end'), and with the scroll lock pinned the newest bubbles must stay visible. Fix in the shared scroll logic (V1 and V2).

Chat area gets a horizontal (side) scroll; never wanted. Find which layout/element overflows (maybe the newest button or long unbroken text/wide cards) in the chat (V1/V2) and the session page as it grows, and fix it: overflow-x hidden, min-width:0 on flex children, word-wrap. Also: the newest button may simply disappear when pinned to the bottom; scroll-locked at bottom is the right picture.

Same bug as the queued 'newest button' fix, new symptom: when a new message arrives and the owner clicks the newest (down-arrow) button, the chat scrolls to a BLANK white area (past the content) and he has to scroll back up. Scroll target must be the bottom of the content (scrollTop = scrollHeight - clientHeight, or the last bubble's bottom edge), never beyond it; check padding/spacer elements and the container that actually scrolls. Merge with the earlier request, one fix.

V1 chat (voice sheet) scrolling jumps around a lot as messages arrive. Needs a proper scroll lock: if the owner is at the bottom (within ~40px) stay pinned to the bottom on new content; if he has scrolled up, never move his position when content is added or re-rendered (preserve scrollTop / anchor to the visible bubble); no jumps on re-render, refinement or reorder. Same shared logic for V2. Combine with the earlier newest-button fixes.

Detail for the scroll fix: the bottom of the LAST bubble should sit a little above the bottom toolbar. Clicking the down-arrow aligns correctly for a second, then it goes wrong again: the scroll position is miscalculated, likely because live (real-time) updates re-render/grow content after the scroll (late height changes, spacers, the toolbar overlay height not subtracted). Fix: scroll to the true bottom minus toolbar height, and keep re-pinning after content growth (ResizeObserver / after render) while pinned. Merge with the earlier scroll requests.

Remove the static 'fast ...' and 'smart ...' text marks shown after the check mark and mic icons under every chat message (V1 and V2). Just delete them from the render (keep any detail as a tooltip only if trivial). Owner has asked for this before; it is noise.

Chat scroll: default mode must be scroll-locked, i.e. automatically stay pinned to the bottom as new content is added (bubbles, streaming text, tasks). Only unlock on a deliberate reader scroll-up gesture; re-lock when the reader returns to the bottom or presses the newest button. Currently scroll position is not working properly at all (jumps, not pinned). Last bubble's bottom should sit just above the toolbar.

Chat v2 Question card (ext/Chat/v2/ChatV2.js + ChatV2.css): it shows two icons, a speech-bubble avatar and a yellow circled question-mark icon. Use the yellow question-mark icon AS the avatar and remove the speech-bubble one (we don't need two icons). Also drop the 'question' and 'open' text labels; the card should just show the question text. (Owner maybe wants a different color for the yellow ? later; leave the color for now.)
Addition to the Chat v2 Question card change: the ? avatar icon shows the question's state. Unanswered question: yellow question mark. Once an answer arrives: it turns green.

Revision to the Question card ? icon (owner said 'maybe', so go with it unless it is hard): three states. Red = asked, not answered. Yellow = answered, not yet read. Green = answered and read (the owner completed it). Replaces the earlier yellow/green two-state version.

Clarifying the Question card read state: tapping the card marks it read, which turns the ? green (red = asked/unanswered, yellow = answered but unread, green = tapped/read). Owner is unsure it is good UI, so keep it simple and easy to undo.

Same as the Question card fix, for the Chat v2 Task card: it has two icons, the speech-bubble-with-three-dots avatar and an empty checkbox next to it. Put the checkbox icon in the avatar slot as the card's one icon and remove the bubble avatar. Also drop the 'task idle' text label (the state is shown by the checkbox).

Task card refinement: the owner is unsure about dropping the state label ('maybe we want a label') and whether an empty checkbox could confuse, but generally the card should go straight into the task's title. Go with: checkbox icon as the avatar, title first, no 'task idle' text; keep it easy to add a small label back.

Question card in Chat v2: the red ? icon now shows (good), but the old speech-bubble avatar still renders next to it, so it must come from somewhere else (probably the shared role/avatar code: ext/Chat/roles.js AVATARS, or a generic avatar in ChatV2.js/ChatV2.css for non-Prompt items). Find where that avatar is drawn for Question (and Task) cards and remove it, so the state icon is the only avatar.

Question card UI (owner decisions): (1) when his spoken sentence becomes a Question card, the plain bubble/sentence it came from is not shown separately any more; only the Question card (hide it in the view only, the data stays in the log). (2) The question title/text is an h3-size heading so it stands out. (3) Flow: he asks, it becomes a question card with the ?, and when answered he knows exactly where to find the answer (answer inside the card). Apply in the chat view where Question cards are drawn (Chat v2; also V1 if the same Question item is drawn there).
